items: Two pages, TIME and REPS: on TIME the clock ends each set, on REPS your reps do.
The last tab sets how a workout ends: after its rounds, on a target, or on a time limit (AMRAP).
Holds: front, reverse and side plank, wall sit, horse stance and handstand. The clock runs only while you hold the position.
5 new exercises: dips, clean & press, thrusters, military press and deadlifts.
Kettlebell reps show which hand did them: L, R, D for both hands on one bell, LR for a bell in each hand.
The Trainer has its own tab for bodyweight, weights and holds, with one card per exercise.
Holds earn ranks too: every 2 seconds held counts as a rep.
Turn the phone sideways to fit your whole body in a tight space.
8 video guides, and spoken hints that explain each page and button the first time.
Your first progress photo's outline guides you back to the same spot.
Fixes: the camera no longer freezes the screen, and recording at 4K 60 no longer crashes.
Camera counting rebuilt: reps count from the front, side or back.
Only the exercise you picked counts, and the app says what it saw.
6 new ready-to-use exercises: burpees, swings, snatches, sit-ups, lunges, jumping jacks.
AMRAP mode, with Cindy and Pushup Test built in.
Runs before or after a workout, measured by GPS.
Moving skeletons show every exercise.
Up to 3 exercises per workout. The Trainer now lists single exercises.
Pick camera or Polar per exercise. With the strap off, the camera takes over.
RankTime is live on the App Store.
TIME and REPS workouts, with Tabata, EMOM, Centurion and Murph built in.
Camera rep counting: train an exercise once and the phone counts your reps.
Heart rate from a Polar H10 or any Bluetooth chest strap, saved to Apple Health.
Record your workout with the timer and your reps shown on the video.
A military rank for every exercise, plus weekly medals for showing up.
History, analytics and progress photos, backed up to your iCloud.

planned.title: Apple Watch app
planned.detail: Run a whole workout from your wrist. Start, pause and finish without touching the phone, see the timer and the current exercise on the watch, and feel every interval change as a tap. Heart rate comes straight off the watch sensor, with no chest strap needed, and the watch motion sensors count your reps, so the camera becomes optional rather than required. Built to work on its own, so you can leave the phone in the bag and still get the full session saved to your history and to Apple Health.
planned.note: This is the next big step for RankTime, and the main thing being worked towards. It is a large build, so it will take time, but the plan is to ship it as one complete app rather than a piece at a time.

planned.title: AirPods rep counting
planned.detail: AirPods with motion sensors can feel your head and upper body move, which is enough to count reps on exercises like push ups, squats and sit ups. That means rep counting without setting up the camera and without wearing anything extra, useful when the phone is in a pocket or the room is too tight to frame yourself.
planned.note: Only AirPods with motion sensors can do this, so older models will not be supported. Accuracy will depend a lot on the exercise, and anything where your head barely moves is unlikely to work well.
